speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: For a nation's economy to function effectively, its citizens must have confidence in its money and payment services.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The Federal Reserve, as the nation's central bank, works to maintain the public's confidence by fostering monetary stability, financial stability, and a safe and efficient payment system.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: This paper is the first step in a public discussion between the Federal Reserve and stakeholders about central bank digital currencies (CBDCs).

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: For the purpose of this paper, a CBDC is defined as a digital liability of a central bank that is widely available to the general public.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: In this respect, it is analogous to a digital form of paper money.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The paper has been designed to foster a broad and transparent public dialogue about CBDCs in general, and about the potential benefits and risks of a U.S. CBDC.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The paper is not intended to advance any specific policy outcome, nor is it intended to signal that the Federal Reserve will make any imminent decisions about the appropriateness of issuing a U.S. CBDC.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Payment technologies offered by the Federal Reserve have evolved over time.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: In the Federal Reserve's early years, it established a national check-clearing system and used dedicated telegraph wires to transfer funds between banks.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: In the 1970s, the Federal Reserve developed an automated clearinghouse (ACH) system that offered an electronic alternative to paper checks.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: And in 2019, the Federal Reserve committed to building the FedNow Service, which will provide real-time, around-the-clock interbank payments, every day of the year.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Recent technological advances have ushered in a wave of new private-sector financial products and services, including digital wallets, mobile payment apps, and new digital assets such as cryptocurrencies and stablecoins.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: These technological advances have also led central banks around the globe to explore the potential benefits and risks of issuing a CBDC.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Federal Reserve policymakers and staff have studied CBDC closely for several years, guided by an understanding that any U.S. CBDC should, among other things

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: provide benefits to households, businesses, and the overall economy that exceed any costs and risks;

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: yield such benefits more effectively than alternative methods;

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: complement, rather than replace, current forms of money and methods for providing financial services;

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: protect consumer privacy;

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: protect against criminal activity; and

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: have broad support from key stakeholders.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The Federal Reserve is committed to soliciting and reviewing a wide range of views as it continues to study whether a U.S. CBDC would be appropriate.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Irrespective of any ultimate conclusion, Federal Reserve staff will continue to play an active role in developing international standards for CBDCs.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: This paper begins with a discussion of existing forms of money; the current state of the U.S. payment system and its relative strengths and challenges; and the various digital assets that have emerged in recent years, including stablecoins and other cryptocurrencies.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The paper then turns to CBDC, focusing on its uses and functions; potential benefits and risks; and related policy considerations.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The Federal Reserve's initial analysis suggests that a potential U.S. CBDC, if one were created, would best serve the needs of the United States by being privacy-protected, intermediated, widely transferable, and identity-verified.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: As noted above, however, the paper is not intended to advance a specific policy outcome and takes no position on the ultimate desirability of a U.S. CBDC.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The Federal Reserve will seek input from a wide range of stakeholders that might use a CBDC or be affected by its introduction.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: This paper concludes with a request for public comment, the first step in a broad consultation that will also include targeted outreach and public forums.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The Federal Reserve is exploring the implications of, and options for, issuing a CBDC.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: For the purpose of this paper, a CBDC is defined as a digital liability of the Federal Reserve that is widely available to the general public.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: While Americans have long held money predominantly in digital form—for example in bank accounts recorded as computer entries on commercial bank ledgers—a CBDC would differ from existing digital money available to the general public because a CBDC would be a liability of the Federal Reserve, not of a commercial bank.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A CBDC could potentially offer a range of benefits.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: For example, it could provide households and businesses a convenient, electronic form of central bank money, with the safety and liquidity that would entail; give entrepreneurs a platform on which to create new financial products and services; support faster and cheaper payments (including cross-border payments); and expand consumer access to the financial system.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A CBDC could also pose certain risks and would raise a variety of important policy questions, including how it might affect financial-sector market structure, the cost and availability of credit, the safety and stability of the financial system, and the efficacy of monetary policy.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The introduction of a CBDC would represent a highly significant innovation in American money.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Accordingly, broad consultation with the general public and key stakeholders is essential.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: This paper is the first step in such a conversation.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: It describes the economic context for a CBDC, key policy considerations, and the potential risks and benefits of a U.S. CBDC.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: It also solicits feedback from all interested parties.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The Federal Reserve does not intend to proceed with issuance of a CBDC without clear support from the executive branch and from Congress, ideally in the form of a specific authorizing law.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Money serves as a means of payment, a store of value, and a unit of account.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: In the United States, money takes multiple forms:

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Central bank money is a liability of the central bank.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: In the United States, central bank money comes in the form of physical currency issued by the Federal Reserve and digital balances held by commercial banks at the Federal Reserve.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Commercial bank money is the digital form of money that is most commonly used by the public.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Commercial bank money is held in accounts at commercial banks.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Nonbank money is digital money held as balances at nonbank financial service providers.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: These firms typically conduct balance transfers on their own books using a range of technologies, including mobile apps.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The different types of money carry different amounts of credit and liquidity risk.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Commercial bank money has very little credit or liquidity risk due to federal deposit insurance, the supervision and regulation of commercial banks, and commercial banks' access to central bank liquidity.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Nonbank money lacks the full range of protections of commercial bank money and therefore generally carries more credit and liquidity risk.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Central bank money carries neither credit nor liquidity risk, and is therefore considered the safest form of money.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Central bank money serves as the foundation of the financial system and the overall economy.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Commercial bank money and nonbank money are denominated in the same units as central bank money (i.e., U.S. dollars) and are intended to be convertible into central bank money.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The U.S. payment system connects a broad range of financial institutions, households, and businesses.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Most payments in the United States rely on interbank payment services—such as the ACH network or wire-transfer systems—to move money from a sender's account at one bank to a recipient's account at another bank.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Accordingly, interbank payment services are critical to the functioning and stability of the financial system and the economy more broadly.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The firms that operate interbank payment services are subject to federal supervision, and systemically important payment firms are subject to heightened supervision and regulation.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Interbank payment systems may initially settle in commercial bank money, or in central bank money, depending on their design.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: However, because central bank money has no credit or liquidity risk, central bank payment systems tend to underpin interbank payments and serve as the backbone of the broader payment system.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The use of central bank money to settle interbank payments promotes financial stability because it eliminates credit and liquidity risk in systemically important payment systems.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Recent improvements to the U.S. payment system have focused on making payments faster, cheaper, more convenient, and more accessible.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: "Instant" payments have been a particularly active field of private- and public-sector innovation.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: For example, The Clearing House has developed the RTP network, which is a real-time interbank payment system for lower-value payments.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The Federal Reserve is also building a new interbank settlement service for instant payments, the FedNow Service, scheduled to debut in 2023.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: These instant payment services will enable commercial banks to provide payment services to households and businesses around the clock, every day of the year, with recipients gaining immediate access to transferred funds.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The growth of these instant payment services also could reduce the costs and fees associated with certain types of payments.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: In addition, a host of consumer-focused services that are accessible through mobile devices have made digital payments faster and more convenient.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Some of these new payment services, however, could pose financial stability, payment system integrity, and other risks.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: For example, if the growth of nonbank payment services were to cause a large-scale shift of money from commercial banks to nonbanks, the resulting lack of equivalent protections that come with commercial bank money could introduce run risk or other instabilities to the financial system.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: While the existing U.S. payment system is generally effective and efficient, certain challenges remain.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: In particular, a significant number of Americans currently lack access to digital banking and payment services.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Additionally, some payments—especially cross-border payments—remain slow and costly.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Digital financial services and commercial bank money have become more accessible over time, and increasing numbers of Americans have opened and maintain bank accounts.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Nonetheless, more than 7 million—or over 5 percent of U.S. households—remain unbanked.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Nearly 20 percent more have bank accounts, but still rely on more costly financial services such as money orders, check-cashing services, and payday loans.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A variety of public- and private-sector efforts are underway to support financial inclusion.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: For example, the private-sector Bank On initiative promotes low-cost, low-risk consumer checking accounts.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta has also formed a Special Committee on Payments Inclusion, a public-private sector collaboration that is working to promote access to digital payments for vulnerable populations.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Cross-border payments currently face a number of challenges, including slow settlement, high fees, and limited accessibility.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The sources of these frictions include the mechanics of currency exchange, variations in different countries' legal regimes and technological infrastructure, timezone complications, and coordination problems among intermediaries, including correspondent banks and nonbank financial service providers.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Regulatory requirements related to money laundering and other illicit activities introduce further complications.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Finally, certain destination countries for cross-border payments have limited competition, allowing existing providers to charge high fees.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: As of the second quarter of 2021, the average cost of sending a remittance from the United States to other countries was 5.41 percent of the notional value of the transaction.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: These high costs have a significant impact on households that make remittance transactions.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: High costs for cross-border payments also affect smaller businesses that make infrequent global payments to suppliers.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Reducing these costs could benefit economic growth, enhance global commerce, improve international remittances, and reduce inequality.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Technological innovation has recently ushered in a wave of digital assets with money-like characteristics.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: These "cryptocurrencies" arose from a combination of cryptographic and distributedledger technologies, which together provide a foundation for decentralized, peer-to-peer payments.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Cryptocurrencies have not been widely adopted as a means of payment in the United States.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: They remain subject to extreme price volatility, are difficult to use without service providers, and have severe limitations on transaction throughput.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Many cryptocurrencies also come with a significant energy footprint and make consumers vulnerable to loss, theft, and fraud.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Stablecoins are a more recent incarnation of cryptocurrency that peg their value to one or more assets, such as a sovereign currency or commodity.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Stablecoins pegged to the U.S. dollar are predominantly used today to facilitate trading of other digital assets, but many firms are exploring ways to promote stablecoins as a widespread means of payment.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A full discussion of stablecoin arrangements is outside the scope of this paper.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: However, the President's Working Group on Financial Markets (PWG), along with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), recently published a report on payment stablecoins.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The PWG report notes that well-designed and appropriately regulated stablecoins could potentially support faster, more efficient, and more inclusive payment options.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The PWG report also notes, however, that the potential for the increased use of stablecoins as a means of payment raises a range of concerns related to the potential for destabilizing runs, disruptions in the payment system, and concentration of economic power.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The PWG report highlights gaps in the authority of regulators to reduce these risks.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: To address the risks of payment stablecoins, the PWG report recommends that Congress act promptly to enact legislation that would ensure payment stablecoins and payment stablecoin arrangements are subject to a consistent and comprehensive federal regulatory framework.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Such legislation would complement existing authorities regarding market integrity, investor protection, and illicit finance.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The Federal Reserve is considering how a CBDC might fit into the U.S. money and payments landscape.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A crucial test for a potential CBDC is whether it would prove superior to other methods that might address issues of concern outlined in this paper.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: As noted above, for the purposes of this discussion paper, CBDC is defined as a digital liability of the Federal Reserve that is widely available to the general public.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Today, Federal Reserve notes (i.e., physical currency) are the only type of central bank money available to the general public.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Like existing forms of commercial bank money and nonbank money, a CBDC would enable the general public to make digital payments.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: As a liability of the Federal Reserve, however, a CBDC would not require mechanisms like deposit insurance to maintain public confidence, nor would a CBDC depend on backing by an underlying asset pool to maintain its value.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A CBDC would be the safest digital asset available to the general public, with no associated credit or liquidity risk.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The Federal Reserve will continue to explore a wide range of design options for a CBDC.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: While no decisions have been made on whether to pursue a CBDC, analysis to date suggests that a potential U.S. CBDC, if one were created, would best serve the needs of the United States by being privacy-protected, intermediated, widely transferable, and identity-verified.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Privacy-protected: Protecting consumer privacy is critical.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Any CBDC would need to strike an appropriate balance, however, between safeguarding the privacy rights of consumers and affording the transparency necessary to deter criminal activity.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Intermediated: The Federal Reserve Act does not authorize direct Federal Reserve accounts for individuals, and such accounts would represent a significant expansion of the Federal Reserve's role in the financial system and the economy.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Under an intermediated model, the private sector would offer accounts or digital wallets to facilitate the management of CBDC holdings and payments.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Potential intermediaries could include commercial banks and regulated nonbank financial service providers, and would operate in an open market for CBDC services.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Although commercial banks and nonbanks would offer services to individuals to manage their CBDC holdings and payments, the CBDC itself would be a liability of the Federal Reserve.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: An intermediated model would facilitate the use of the private sector's existing privacy and identity-management frameworks; leverage the private sector's ability to innovate; and reduce the prospects for destabilizing disruptions to the well-functioning U.S. financial system.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Transferable: For a CBDC to serve as a widely accessible means of payment, it would need to be readily transferable between customers of different intermediaries.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The ability to transfer value seamlessly between different intermediaries makes the payment system more efficient by allowing money to move freely throughout the economy.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Identity-verified: Financial institutions in the United States are subject to robust rules that are designed to combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A CBDC would need to be designed to comply with these rules.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: In practice, this would mean that a CBDC intermediary would need to verify the identity of a person accessing CBDC, just as banks and other financial institutions currently verify the identities of their customers.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: CBDC transactions would need to be final and completed in real time, allowing users to make payments to one another using a risk-free asset.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Individuals, businesses, and governments could potentially use a CBDC to make basic purchases of goods and services or pay bills, and governments could use a CBDC to collect taxes or make benefit payments directly to citizens.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Additionally, a CBDC could potentially be programmed to, for example, deliver payments at certain times.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A CBDC could potentially serve as a new foundation for the payment system and a bridge between different payment services, both legacy and new.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: It could also maintain the centrality of safe and trusted central bank money in a rapidly digitizing economy.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A U.S. CBDC would offer the general public broad access to digital money that is free from credit risk and liquidity risk.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: As such, it could provide a safe foundation for private-sector innovations to meet current and future needs and demands for payment services.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: All options for private digital money, including stablecoins and other cryptocurrencies, require mechanisms to reduce liquidity risk and credit risk.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: But all these mechanisms are imperfect.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: In our rapidly digitizing economy, the proliferation of private digital money could present risks to both individual users and the financial system as a whole.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A U.S. CBDC could mitigate some of these risks while supporting private-sector innovation.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A CBDC might also help to level the playing field in payment innovation for private-sector firms of all sizes.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: For some smaller firms, the costs and risks of issuing a safe and robust form of private money may be prohibitive.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A CBDC could overcome this barrier and allow private-sector innovators to focus on new access services, distribution methods, and related service offerings.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Finally, a CBDC might generate new capabilities to meet the evolving speed and efficiency requirements of the digital economy.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: As noted above, for example, a CBDC could potentially be programmed to deliver payments at certain times.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Additionally, a CBDC could potentially be used to carry out micropayments—financial transactions that usually occur online and involve very small sums of money—which traditional payment systems are not necessarily designed to facilitate.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: CBDC has the potential to streamline cross-border payments by using new technologies, introducing simplified distribution channels, and creating additional opportunities for crossjurisdictional collaboration and interoperability.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Realizing these potential improvements would require significant international coordination to address issues such as common standards and infrastructure, the types of intermediaries that would be able to access any new infrastructure, legal frameworks, preventing illicit transactions, and the cost and timing of implementation.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Another potential benefit of a U.S.-issued CBDC could be to preserve the dominant international role of the U.S. dollar.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The dollar is the world's most widely used currency for payments and investments; it also serves as the world's reserve currency.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The dollar's international role benefits the United States by, among other things, lowering transaction and borrowing costs for U.S. households, businesses, and government.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The dollar's international role also allows the United States to influence standards for the global monetary system.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Today, the dollar is widely used across the globe because of the depth and liquidity of U.S. financial markets, the size and openness of the U.S. economy, and international trust in U.S. institutions and rule of law.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: It is important, however, to consider the implications of a potential future state in which many foreign countries and currency unions may have introduced CBDCs.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Some have suggested that, if these new CBDCs were more attractive than existing forms of the U.S. dollar, global use of the dollar could decrease—and a U.S. CBDC might help preserve the international role of the dollar.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Promoting financial inclusion—particularly for economically vulnerable households and communities—is a high priority for the Federal Reserve.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Private-sector electronic transactions accounts facilitate access to digital payments; enable rapid and cost-effective payment of taxes; enable rapid and cost-effective delivery of wages, tax refunds, and other federal payments; provide a secure way for people to save; and promote access to credit.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Some have suggested that a CBDC could reduce common barriers to financial inclusion and could lower transaction costs, which could be particularly helpful for lower-income households.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Further study would be helpful to assess the potential for CBDC to expand financial inclusion, including cases targeted to underserved and lower income households.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Cash is currently the only central bank money that is available to the general public, and it remains an important and popular means of payment.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: According to a 2020 survey, U.S. consumers used cash for 19 percent of total transactions (6 percent by value).

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The Federal Reserve is committed to ensuring the continued safety and availability of cash and is considering a CBDC as a means to expand safe payment options, not to reduce or replace them.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: In some jurisdictions, however, digital payments have rapidly supplanted cash.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: While cash use in the United States fell from 40 percent of transactions in 2012 (12 percent by value) to 19 percent in 2020, other countries have seen more rapid declines.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: In Sweden, for example, the proportion of cash payments fell from 33 percent to less than 10 percent over the same period.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: In China, 50 percent of point-of-sale (POS) payments are made with a mobile wallet or app, while cash accounts for just 13 percent of POS payments.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: If these trends were to emerge in the United States, consumers might want the option of digitized central bank money that, like cash, would have no credit or liquidity risk attached to it.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Although the introduction of a CBDC could benefit U.S. consumers and the broader financial system, it would also raise complex policy issues and risks.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Each of the issues described below will require additional research and analysis.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A CBDC could fundamentally change the structure of the U.S. financial system, altering the roles and responsibilities of the private sector and the central bank.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Banks currently rely (in large part) on deposits to fund their loans.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A widely available CBDC would serve as a close—or, in the case of an interest-bearing CBDC, near-perfect—substitute for commercial bank money.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: This substitution effect could reduce the aggregate amount of deposits in the banking system, which could in turn increase bank funding expenses, and reduce credit availability or raise credit costs for households and businesses.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Similarly, an interest-bearing CBDC could result in a shift away from other low-risk assets, such as shares in money market mutual funds, Treasury bills, and other short-term instruments.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A shift away from these other low-risk assets could reduce credit availability or raise credit costs for businesses and governments.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: These concerns could potentially be mitigated by CBDC design choices.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A non-interest-bearing CBDC, for example, would be less attractive as a substitute for commercial bank money.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: In addition, a central bank might limit the amount of CBDC an end user could hold.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: A CBDC could spur innovation by banks and other actors and would be a safer deposit substitute than many other products, including stablecoins and other types of nonbank money.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: These forms of nonbank money could cause a shift in deposits away from banks even without a CBDC.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Because central bank money is the safest form of money, a widely accessible CBDC would be particularly attractive to risk-averse users, especially during times of stress in the financial system.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: The ability to quickly convert other forms of money—including deposits at commercial banks—into CBDC could make runs on financial firms more likely or more severe.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: Traditional measures such as prudential supervision, government deposit insurance, and access to central bank liquidity may be insufficient to stave off large outflows of commercial bank deposits into CBDC in the event of financial panic.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: As with concerns related to financial-sector market structure, some of these flight-to-safety concerns could potentially be mitigated by CBDC design choices.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sentence: For example, a central bank could pay no interest on CBDC.

speaker: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In all this excitement, there are also calls for the Federal Reserve to "get in the game" and issue a central bank digital currency (CBDC) that the general public could use.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Chair Powell recently announced that the Federal Reserve will publish a discussion paper on the benefits and costs of creating a CBDC.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: This topic is of special interest to me, since I have worked on monetary theory for the last twenty years and researched and written about alternative forms of money for the last seven.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: My speech today focuses on whether a CBDC would address any major problems affecting our payment system.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: There are also potential risks associated with a CBDC, and I will touch on those at the end of my remarks.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: But at this early juncture in the Fed's discussions, I think the first order of business is to ask whether there is compelling need for the Fed to create a digital currency.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I am highly skeptical.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In all the recent exuberance about CBDCs, advocates point to many potential benefits of a Federal Reserve digital currency, but they often fail to ask a simple question: What problem would a CBDC solve?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Alternatively, what market failure or inefficiency demands this specific intervention?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: After careful consideration, I am not convinced as of yet that a CBDC would solve any existing problem that is not being addressed more promptly and efficiently by other initiatives.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Before getting into the details, let me start by clarifying what I mean by "CBDC."

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Put simply, a CBDC is a liability of the central bank that can be used as a digital payment instrument.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: For purposes of this speech, I will focus on general purpose CBDCs—that is, CBDCs that could be used by the general public, not just by banks or other specific types of institutions.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: A general purpose CBDC could potentially take many forms, some of which could act as anonymous cash-like payment instruments.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: For this speech, however, I will focus on account-based forms of CBDC, which the Bank for International Settlements recently described as "the most promising way of providing central bank money in the digital age."

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Any such general purpose, account-based CBDC would likely require explicit congressional authorization.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Central Bank Money versus Commercial Bank Money It is useful to note that in our daily lives we use both central bank money and commercial bank money for transactions.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Central bank money (i.e., money that is a liability of the Federal Reserve) includes physical currency held by the general public and digital account balances held by banks at the Federal Reserve.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The funds banks put into these accounts are called reserve balances, which are used to clear and settle payments between banks.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In contrast, checking and savings accounts at commercial banks are liabilities of the banks, not the Federal Reserve.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The bulk of transactions, by value, that U.S. households and firms make each day use commercial bank money as the payment instrument.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Federal Reserve Accounts and Commercial Bank Accounts Under current law, the Federal Reserve offers accounts and payment services to commercial banks.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: These accounts provide a risk-free settlement asset for trillions of dollars of daily interbank payments.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Importantly, the use of central bank money to settle interbank payments promotes financial stability because it eliminates credit and liquidity risk in systemically important payment systems.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Congress did not establish the Federal Reserve to provide accounts directly to the general public; the Federal Reserve instead works in the background by providing accounts to commercial banks, which then provide bank accounts to the general public.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Under this structure, commercial banks act as an intermediary between the Federal Reserve and the general public.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The funds in commercial bank accounts are digital and can be used to make digital payments to households and businesses, but commercial banks promise to redeem a dollar in one's bank account into $1 of U.S. currency.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In short, banks peg the exchange rate between commercial bank money and the U.S. dollar at one-to-one.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Due to substantial regulatory and supervisory oversight and federal deposit insurance, households and firms reasonably view this fixed exchange rate as perfectly credible.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Consequently, they treat commercial bank money and central bank money as perfect substitutes—they are interchangeable as a means of payment.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The credibility of this fixed exchange rate between commercial and central bank money is what allows our payment system to be stable and efficient.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I will return to this point later.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: This division of functions between the Federal Reserve and commercial banks reflects an economic truth: that markets operate efficiently when private-sector firms compete to provide the highest-quality products to consumers and businesses at the lowest possible cost.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In general, the government should compete with the private sector only to address market failures.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Consideration of the Case for a Federal Reserve CBDC This brings us back to my original question: What is the problem with our current payment system that only a CBDC would solve?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could it be that physical currency will disappear?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: As I mentioned before, the key to having credible commercial bank money is the promise that banks will convert a dollar of digital bank money into a dollar of U.S. physical currency.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: But how can banks deliver on their promise if U.S. currency disappears?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Accordingly, many central banks are considering adoption of a CBDC as their economies become "cashless."

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Eliminating currency is a policy choice, however, not an economic outcome, and Chair Powell has made clear that U.S. currency is not going to be replaced by a CBDC.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Thus, a fear of imminently vanishing physical currency cannot be the reason for adopting a CBDC.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could it be that the payment system is too limited in reach, and that introducing a CBDC would make the payment system bigger, broader, and more efficient?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It certainly doesn't look that way to me.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Our existing interbank payment services have nationwide reach, meaning that an accountholder at one commercial bank can make a payment to an accountholder at any other U.S. bank.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The same applies to international payments—accountholders at U.S. banks can transfer funds abroad to accountholders at foreign banks.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: So, a lack of connectedness and geographic breadth in the U.S. payment system is not a good reason to introduce a CBDC.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could it be that existing payment services are too slow?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: A group of commercial banks has recently developed an instant payment service (the Real-Time Payment Service, or RTP), and the Federal Reserve is creating its own instant payment service, FedNowSM.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: These services will move funds between accountholders at U.S. commercial banks immediately after a payment is initiated.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: While cross-border payments are typically less efficient than domestic payments, efforts are underway to improve cross-border payments as well.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: These innovations are all moving forward in the absence of a CBDC.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Consequently, facilitating speedier payments is not a compelling reason to create a CBDC.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could it be that too few people can access the payment system?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Some argue that introducing a CBDC would improve financial inclusion by allowing the unbanked to more readily access financial services.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: To address this argument, we need to know, first, the size of the unbanked population, and second, whether the unbanked population would use a Federal Reserve CBDC account.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: According to a recent Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) survey, approximately 5.4 percent of U.S. households were unbanked in 2019.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The FDIC survey also found that approximately 75 percent of the unbanked population "were not at all interested" or "not very interested" in having a bank account.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: If the same percentage of the unbanked population would not be interested in a Federal Reserve CBDC account, this means that a little more than 1 percent of U.S. households are both unbanked and potentially interested in a Federal Reserve CBDC account.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It is implausible to me that developing a CBDC is the simplest, least costly way to reach this 1 percent of households.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Instead, we could promote financial inclusion more efficiently by, for example, encouraging widespread use of low-cost commercial bank accounts through the Cities for Financial Empowerment Bank On project.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could it be that a CBDC is needed because existing payment services are unreasonably expensive?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In order to answer this question, we need to understand why the price charged for a payment might be considered "high."

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In economics, the price of a service is typically composed of two parts: the marginal cost of providing the service and a markup that reflects the market power of the seller.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The marginal cost of processing a payment depends on the nature of the payment (for example, paper check versus electronic transfer), the technology used (for example, batched payments versus real-time payments), and the other services provided in processing the payment (for example, risk and fraud services).

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Since these factors are primarily technological, and there is no reason to think that the Federal Reserve can develop cheaper technology than private firms, it seems unlikely that the Federal Reserve would be able to process CBDC payments at a materially lower marginal cost than existing private-sector payment services.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The key question, then, is how a CBDC would affect the markup charged by banks for a variety of payment services.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The markup that a firm can charge depends on its market power and thus the degree of competition it faces.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Introducing a CBDC would create additional competition in the market for payment services, because the general public could use CBDC accounts to make payments directly through the Federal Reserve—that is, a CBDC would allow the general public to bypass the commercial banking system.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Deposits would flow from commercial banks into CBDC accounts, which would put pressure on banks to lower their fees, or raise the interest rate paid on deposits, to prevent additional deposit outflows.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It seems to me, however, that private-sector innovations might reduce the markup charged by banks more effectively than a CBDC would.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: If commercial banks are earning rents from their market power, then there is a profit opportunity for nonbanks to enter the payment business and provide the general public with cheaper payment services.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: And, indeed, we are currently seeing a surge of nonbanks getting into payments.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: For example, in recent years, "stablecoin" arrangements have emerged as a particularly important type of nonbank entrant into the payments landscape.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Stablecoins are digital assets whose value is tied to one or more other assets, such as a sovereign currency.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: A stablecoin could serve as an attractive payment instrument if it is pegged one-to-one to the dollar and is backed by a safe and liquid pool of assets.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: If one or more stablecoin arrangements can develop a significant user base, they could become a major challenger to banks for processing payments.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Importantly, payments using such stablecoins might be "free" in the sense that there would be no fee required to initiate or receive a payment.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Accordingly, one can easily imagine that competition from stablecoins could pressure banks to reduce their markup for payment services.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Please note that I am not endorsing any particular stablecoin—some of which are not backed by safe and liquid assets.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The promise of redemption of a stablecoin into one U.S. dollar is not perfectly credible, nor have they been tested by an actual run on the stablecoin.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: There are many legal, regulatory, and policy issues that need to be resolved before stablecoins can safely proliferate.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: My point, however, is that the private sector is already developing payment alternatives to compete with the banking system.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Hence, it seems unnecessary for the Federal Reserve to create a CBDC to drive down payment rents.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Returning to possible problems a CBDC could solve, it is often argued that the creation of a CBDC would spur innovation in the payment system.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: This leads me to ask: do we think there is insufficient innovation going on in payments?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: To the contrary, it seems to me that private-sector innovation is occurring quite rapidly—in fact, faster than regulators can process.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: So, spurring innovation is not a compelling reason to introduce a CBDC.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could it be, however, that the types of innovations being pursued by the private sector are the "wrong" types of payment innovations?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I see some merit in this argument when I consider crypto-assets such as bitcoin that are often used to facilitate illicit activity.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: But a CBDC is unlikely to deter the use of crypto-assets that are designed to evade governmental oversight.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could the problem be that government authorities have insufficient information regarding the financial transactions of U.S. citizens?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In general, the government has sought to balance individuals' right to privacy with the need to prevent illicit financial transactions, such as money laundering.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: For example, while the government does not receive all transaction data regarding accountholders at commercial banks, the Bank Secrecy Act requires that commercial banks report suspicious activity to the government.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Depending on its design, CBDC accounts could give the Federal Reserve access to a vast amount of information regarding the financial transactions and trading patterns of CBDC accountholders.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The introduction of a CBDC in China, for example, likely will allow the Chinese government to more closely monitor the economic activity of its citizens.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Should the Federal Reserve create a CBDC for the same reason?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I, for one, do not think so.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Could the problem be that the reserve currency status of the U.S. dollar is at risk and the creation of a Federal Reserve CBDC is needed to maintain the primacy of the U.S. dollar?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Some commentators have expressed concern, for example, that the availability of a Chinese CBDC will undermine the status of the U.S. dollar.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I see no reason to expect that the world will flock to a Chinese CBDC or any other.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Why would non-Chinese firms suddenly desire to have all their financial transactions monitored by the Chinese government?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Why would this induce non-Chinese firms to denominate their contracts and trading activities in the Chinese currency instead of the U.S. dollar?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Additionally, I fail to see how allowing U.S. households to, for example, pay their electric bills via a Federal Reserve CBDC account instead of a commercial bank account would help to maintain global dollar supremacy.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: (Of course, Federal Reserve CBDC accounts that are available to persons outside the United States might promote use of the dollar, but global availability of Federal Reserve CBDC accounts would also raise acute problems related to, among other things, money laundering.)

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Finally, could it be that new forms of private money, such as stablecoins, represent a threat to the Federal Reserve for conducting monetary policy?

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Many commentators have suggested that new private monies will diminish the impact of the Federal Reserve's policy actions, since they will act as competing monetary systems.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: It is well established in international economics that any country that pegs its exchange rate to the U.S. dollar surrenders its domestic monetary policy to the United States and imports U.S. monetary policy.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: This same logic applies to any entity that pegs its exchange rate to the U.S. dollar.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: Consequently, commercial banks and stablecoins pegged to the U.S. dollar act as conduits for U.S. monetary policy and amplify policy actions.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: So, if anything, private stablecoins pegged to the dollar broaden the reach of U.S. monetary policy rather than diminish it.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: After exploring many possible problems that a CBDC could solve, I am left with the conclusion that a CBDC remains a solution in search of a problem.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: That leaves us only with more philosophical reasons to adopt a CBDC.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: One could argue, for example, that the general public has a fundamental right to hold a riskless digital payment instrument, and a CBDC would do this in a way no privately issued payment instrument can.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: On the other hand, thanks to federal deposit insurance, commercial bank accounts already offer the general public a riskless digital payment instrument for the vast majority of transactions.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: One could also argue that the Federal Reserve should provide a digital option as an alternative to the commercial banking system.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The argument is that the government should not force its citizens to use the commercial banking system, but should instead allow access to the central bank as a public service available to all.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: As I noted earlier in my speech, however, the current congressionally mandated division of functions between the Federal Reserve and commercial banks reflects an understanding that, in general, the government should compete with the private sector only to address market failures.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: This bedrock principle has stood America in good stead since its founding, and I don't think that CBDCs are the case for making an exception.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: In summary, while CBDCs continue to generate enormous interest in the United States and other countries, I remain skeptical that a Federal Reserve CBDC would solve any major problem confronting the U.S. payment system.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: There are also potential costs and risks associated with a CBDC, some of which I have alluded to already.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I have noted my belief that government interventions into the economy should come only to address significant market failures.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: The competition of a Fed CBDC could disintermediate commercial banks and threaten a division of labor in the financial system that works well.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: And, as cybersecurity concerns mount, a CBDC could become a new target for those threats.

speaker: Christopher J. Waller
sentence: I expect these and other potential risks from a CBDC will be addressed in the forthcoming discussion paper, and I intend to expand upon them as the debate over digital currencies moves forward.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The financial system is undergoing fast-moving changes associated with digitalization and decentralization.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Some of these innovations hold considerable promise to reduce transaction costs and frictions, increase competition, and improve financial inclusion, but there are also potential risks.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: With technology driving profound change, it is important we prepare for the financial system of the future and not limit our thinking to the financial system of today.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The Evolving Digitalization and Decentralization of Finance In recent years, there has been explosive growth in the development and adoption of new digital assets that leverage distributed ledger technologies and cryptography.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The market capitalization of cryptocurrencies grew from less than $100 billion five years ago to a high of almost $3 trillion in November 2021 and is currently around $2 trillion.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In parallel, we have seen rapid growth in the platforms that facilitate the crypto finance ecosystem, including decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: These crypto platforms facilitate a variety of activities, including lending, trading, and custodying crypto-assets, in some cases outside the traditional regulatory guardrails for investor and consumer protection, market integrity, and transparency.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The growth in the crypto finance ecosystem is fueling demand for stablecoins—digital assets that are intended to maintain stable value relative to reference assets, such as the U.S. dollar.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Stablecoin supply grew nearly sixfold in 2021, from roughly $29 billion in January 2021 to $165 billion in January 2022.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: There is a high degree of concentration among a few dollar-pegged stablecoins: As of January 2022, the largest stablecoin by market capitalization made up almost half of the market, and the four largest stablecoins together made up almost 90 percent.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Today, stablecoins are being used as collateral on DeFi and other crypto platforms, as well as in facilitating trading and monetization of cryptocurrency positions on and between crypto and other platforms.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In the future, some issuers envision that stablecoins will also have an expanded reach in the payment system and be commonly used for everyday transactions, both domestic and cross-border.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: So it is important to have strong frameworks for the quality and sufficiency of reserves and risk management and governance.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: As noted in a recent report on stablecoins by the President's Working Group on Financial Markets, it is important to guard against run risk, whereby the prospect of an issuer not being able to promptly and adequately meet redemption requests for the stablecoin at par could result in a sudden surge in redemption demand.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: It is also important to address settlement risk, whereby funds settlement is not certain and final when expected, and systemic risk, whereby the failure or distress of a stablecoin provider could adversely affect the broader financial system.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The prominence of crypto advertisements during the Super Bowl highlighted the growing engagement of retail investors in the crypto ecosystem.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In late 2021, Pew Research found that 16 percent of survey respondents reported having personally invested in, traded, or otherwise used a cryptocurrency—up from less than 1 percent of respondents in 2015.7 There is also rising interest among institutional investors.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: So it is perhaps not surprising that established financial intermediaries are undertaking efforts to expand the crypto services and products they offer.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: If the past year is any guide, the crypto financial system is likely to continue to grow and evolve in ways that increase interconnectedness with the traditional financial system.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: As a result, officials in many countries are undertaking efforts to understand and adapt to the transformation of the financial system.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Many jurisdictions are making efforts to ensure statutory and regulatory frameworks apply like rules to like risks, and some jurisdictions are issuing or contemplating issuing central bank currency in digital form.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Preparing for the Payment System of the Future The Federal Reserve needs to be preparing for the payment landscape of the future even as we continue to make improvements to meet today's needs.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In light of the rapid digitalization of the financial system, the Federal Reserve has been thinking critically about whether there is a role for a potential U.S. central bank digital currency (CBDC) in the digital payment landscape of the future and about its potential properties, costs, and benefits.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Our financial and payment system delivers important benefits today and is continuing to improve with developments like real-time payments.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Nonetheless, certain challenges remain, such as a lack of access to digital banking and payment services for some Americans and expensive and slow cross-border payments.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Growing interest in the digital financial ecosystem suggests that technology is enabling potential improvements that merit consideration.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In addition, it is important to consider how new forms of crypto-assets and digital money may affect the Federal Reserve's responsibilities to maintain financial stability, a safe and efficient payment system, household and business access to safe central bank money, and maximum employment and price stability.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: It is prudent to explore whether there is a role for a CBDC to preserve some of the safe and effective elements of the financial system of the present in a way that is complementary to the private sector innovations transforming the financial landscape of the future.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The public and private sector play important complementary roles within the financial system in the United States.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: From Fedwire to FedNow, the Federal Reserve has over a century of experience working to improve the infrastructure of the U.S. payment system to provide a resilient and adaptable foundation for dynamic private sector activity.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In parallel, private sector banks and nonbanks have competed to build the best possible products and services on top of that foundation and to meet the dollar-denominated needs of consumers and investors at home and around the world.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The result is a resilient payment system that is responsive to the changing needs of businesses, consumers, and investors.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: While the official sector provides a stable currency, operates some important payment rails, and undertakes regulation and oversight of financial intermediaries and critical financial market infrastructures, the private sector brings competitive forces encouraging efficiency and new product offerings and driving innovation.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Responsible innovation has the potential to increase financial inclusion and efficiency and to lower costs within guardrails that protect consumers and investors and safeguard financial stability.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: As we assess the range of future states of the financial system, it is prudent to consider how to preserve ready public access to government-issued, risk-free currency in the digital financial system—the digital equivalent of the Federal Reserve's issuance of physical currency.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The Board recently issued a discussion paper that outlines the Federal Reserve's current thinking on the potential benefits, risks, and policy considerations of a U.S. CBDC.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The paper does not advance any specific policy outcome and does not signal that the Board will make any imminent decisions about the appropriateness of issuing a U.S. CBDC.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: It lays out four CBDC design principles that analysis to date suggests would best serve the needs of the United States if one were created.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Those principles are that a potential CBDC should be privacy-protected, so consumer data and privacy are safeguarded; intermediated, such that financial intermediaries rather than the Federal Reserve interface directly with consumers; widely transferable, so the payment system is not fragmented; and identity-verified, so law enforcement can continue to combat money laundering and funding of terrorism.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Financial Stability Given the Federal Reserve's mandate to promote financial stability, any consideration of a CBDC must include a robust evaluation of its impact on the stability of the financial system—not only as it exists today but also as it may evolve in the future.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In consideration of the financial system today, it would be important to explore design features that would ensure complementarity with established financial intermediation.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: A CBDC—depending on its features—could be attractive as a store of value and means of payment to the extent it is seen as the safest form of money.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: This could make it attractive to risk-averse users, perhaps leading to increased demand for the CBDC at the expense of other intermediaries during times of stress.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: So it is important to undertake research regarding the tools and design features that could be introduced to limit such risks, such as offering a non-interest bearing CBDC and limiting the amount of CBDC an end user could hold or transfer.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: As I noted at the start, the digital asset and payment ecosystem is evolving at a rapid pace.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Thus, it is also important to contemplate the potential role of a CBDC to promote financial stability in a future financial system in which a growing range of consumer payment and financial transactions would be conducted via digital currencies such as stablecoins.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: If current trends continue, the stablecoin market in the future could come to be dominated by just one or two issuers.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Depending on the characteristics of these stablecoins, there could be large shifts in desired holdings between these stablecoins and deposits, leading to large-scale redemptions by risk-averse users at times of stress that could prove disruptive to financial stability.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In such a future state, the coexistence of CBDC alongside stablecoins and commercial bank money could prove complementary, by providing a safe central bank liability in the digital financial ecosystem, much like cash currently coexists with commercial bank money.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: It is essential that policymakers, including the Federal Reserve, plan for the future of the payment system and consider the full range of possible options to bring forward the potential benefits of new technologies, while safeguarding stability.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: International Considerations Analysis of the potential future state of the financial system is not limited to the domestic implications.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The dollar is important to global financial markets: It is not only the predominant global reserve currency, but the dollar is also the most widely used currency in international payments.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Decisions by other major jurisdictions to issue CBDCs could bring important changes to global financial markets that may prove more or less disruptive and that could influence the potential risks and benefits of a U.S. CBDC.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Thus, it is wise to consider what the future states of global financial markets and transactions would look like both with and without a Federal Reserve-issued CBDC.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: For example, the People's Bank of China has been piloting the digital yuan, also known as e-CNY, in numerous Chinese cities over the past two years.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The substantial early progress on the digital yuan may have implications for the evolution of cross-border payments and payment systems.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: And it may influence the development of norms and standards for cross-border digital financial transactions.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: It is prudent to consider how the potential absence or issuance of a U.S. CBDC could affect the use of the dollar in payments globally in future states where one or more major foreign currencies are issued in CBDC form.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: A U.S. CBDC may be one potential way to ensure that people around the world who use the dollar can continue to rely on the strength and safety of U.S. currency to transact and conduct business in the digital financial system.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: More broadly, it is important to consider how the United States can continue to play a lead role in the development of standards governing international digital financial transactions involving CBDCs consistent with norms such as privacy and security.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Given the dollar's important role as a payment instrument across the world, it is essential that the United States be on the frontier of research and policy development regarding CBDC, as international developments related to CBDC can have implications for the global financial system.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Technology Research and Experimentation Given the range of possible future states with significant digitization of the financial system, it is important that the Federal Reserve is actively engaging with the underlying technologies.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Our work to build 24x7x365 instant payments rails leverages lessons from some of today's most resilient, high-performing, and large-scale technology platforms across the globe.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: It is providing important insights on the clearing and settlement models associated with real time payments as well as on fraud, cyber resilience, cloud computing, and related technologies.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In parallel with the Board's public consultation on CBDC, the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, in collaboration with the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, has developed a theoretical high-performance transaction processor for CBDC.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: They recently published the resulting software under an open-source license as a way of engaging with the broader technical community and promoting transparency and verifiability.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Moreover, the Board is studying how innovations, such as distributed ledger technology, could improve the financial system.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: This work includes experimentation with stablecoin interoperability and testing of retail payments across multiple distributed payment ledger systems.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York recently established an Innovation Center, focused on validating, designing, building, and launching new financial technology products and services for the central bank community.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: These technology research and development initiatives are vital to our responsibilities to promote a safe and efficient payment system and financial stability, whatever the future may bring.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Conclusion The financial system is not standing still, and neither can we.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: The digital financial ecosystem is evolving rapidly and becoming increasingly connected with the traditional financial system.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: It is prudent for the Board to understand the evolving payment landscape, the technological advancements and consumer demands driving this evolution, and the consequent policy choices as it seeks to fulfill its congressionally-mandated role to promote a safe, efficient, and inclusive system for U.S. dollar transactions.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: To prepare for the financial system of the future, the Federal Reserve is engaging in research and experimentation with these new technologies and consulting closely with public and private sector partners.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: Chairwoman Waters, Ranking Member McHenry, and other members of the Committee, I am pleased to join you today.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: With technology driving profound change, it is important we prepare for the financial system of the future and not limit our thinking to the financial system of today.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: No decision has been made about whether a U.S. central bank digital currency (CBDC) will be a part of that future, but it is important to undertake the necessary work to inform any such decision and to be ready to move forward should the need arise.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: There has been explosive growth in an emergent digital financial system built around new digital assets and facilitated by crypto-asset platforms and stablecoins as settlement assets.

speaker: Lael Brainard
sentence: In recent weeks, two widely used stablecoins have come under considerable pressure.

speaker: Lael Brainard
